reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a robust, piecewise-constant staircase pattern with a fundamental period of ~95 points (1 cycle), confirmed by the estimated period and window_cycles scaling. Each cycle consists of a flat plateau followed by a sharp downward step (~0.2–0.3 standardized units), then another plateau; occasional upward steps occur but are rarer and smaller. The overall trend is near-zero slope across long horizons (slope_per_point ≈ ±0.0006), indicating trend-stationarity. Amplitude (90th percentile range) varies between 1.18–1.91, reflecting baseline shifts rather than intrinsic amplitude modulation. Peaks are flat-topped plateaus with abrupt vertical transitions; troughs are similarly flat but lower. Noise is minimal—roughness and curvature are zero in catalog, and visual inspection shows no high-frequency jitter; minor spiky deviations (<0.2 units) appear only in candidates 1 and 2 near mid-cycle and are likely measurement artifacts or transient micro-events, not structural anomalies. Baseline level drifts across segments: candidate 0 is centered near −0.75, candidate 1 near −0.15, candidate 2 near +0.85, candidate 3 near −0.65—this reflects global level shifts, not local anomalies. All candidates share identical morphological motifs: plateau → drop → plateau → (occasional small rise) → repeat. Acceptable variation includes ±0.3 shift in median, ±0.15 in MAD, and presence of isolated sub-0.2 spikes; deviations beyond this (e.g., prolonged non-flat segments, irregular step sizes, or >0.5 slope per point) would be suspect.

Three-cycle (285-point) segment with same staircase motif but includes two small, narrow upward spikes (~0.2 units) around indices 880 and 990. Baseline is higher (median −0.17). Plateaus and drops remain consistent; spikes are localized and do not disrupt cycle structure.

Three-cycle segment with highest baseline (median +0.84), showing identical staircase shape. Contains one small spike near index 1840 and a slightly asymmetric drop around 1835–1840. Overall morphology matches candidate 1 closely; level shift is the main difference.

Five-cycle (475-point) segment spanning longer horizon; staircase continues faithfully with same step depth and plateau duration. Includes a brief dip to −2.0 around index 2725, but recovers immediately—consistent with deeper troughs seen in other candidates. No spikes; noise-free. Best for assessing long-range stability.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for queries with single-cycle length or when high fidelity to canonical morphology is needed (e.g., detecting subtle step distortions). Use reference 3 for multi-cycle queries (>3 cycles) to assess phase coherence and long-term drift. Reference 1 and 2 are acceptable for 3-cycle queries but downweight if query lacks their minor spikes—those spikes are not part of core normal pattern and may indicate local perturbation. When query shows elevated baseline, align with candidate 2’s level; for depressed baseline, align with candidate 0 or 3.
uncertainties: Exact step height tolerance: catalog amplitude_90 varies by ~0.7 units across candidates; unclear whether this reflects true normal variability or dataset-level scaling artifacts.

Whether the rare upward spikes in candidates 1 and 2 are permissible noise or low-grade anomalies—consensus treats them as noise due to isolation and small magnitude, but reliability is reduced accordingly.
